requirements.text: Build the visual world around the arc stress → stillness → restoration → energy; the product should feel like a reset, not a generic sleep aid.
Keep each execution focused: one hero visual, one hero message, one brand cue and one CTA.
Use calm, domestic, edited spaces with natural light and integrated greenery; avoid theatrical or cluttered showroom-like settings.
Show believable human behaviour with soft hands, real stretch, calm connection and relaxed homewear; avoid presenter poses and exaggerated smiles.
Preserve product truth in retouching and proof: keep fabric texture, skin truth, daylight variation and natural shadows; do not flatten the product into plastic-looking polish.
Treat red as a controlled signal, not a room-flooding colour; avoid red curtains, bedding, props or outfits in room scenes.
Plan every launch as an asset system, not a single hero image: icon, inhabited hero, world, intelligence, performance and sale outputs are required.
Keep strategy language distinct from proof; do not turn positioning copy into efficacy claims without product-specific approved substantiation.

preferences.text: Warm neutral, tactile domestic interiors read as the strongest recurring world; wood, stone, linen and soft plaster are the most compatible supporting cues.
Large openings, visible floor area and clear circulation make the room feel calmer and more premium than dense styling.
Daylight-led mattress and pillow worlds feel most native; sofas and recliners can carry warmer, lower-light evening moods.
The product reads best when it stays central with breathing room rather than being buried in busy compositions.
Observed executions favour an Indian modern domestic tone over hotel-luxury or clinical-tech extremes.
Controlled red accents and mixed category thumbnails appear in current official web practice, but should remain channel-specific rather than universal.
The draft visual world repeatedly favours calm, tactile, human scenes with relaxed gestures and ordinary home rituals.
Typography is not fully resolved across sources; the final system should be confirmed before production.

visualRules.value: Use one hero visual, one hero message, one brand cue and one CTA.
Keep ample breathing room; the product should sit in a calm centre rather than a crowded frame.
Show believable human behaviour: closed eyes, soft hands, real stretch, calm connection, leaning, reclining or reading; avoid presenter poses and exaggerated smiles.
Use soft homewear with relaxed silhouettes and muted tones; avoid partywear, loud prints, synthetic shine and branded athleisure.
Rooms should rely on quiet surfaces, edited styling, natural light and integrated greenery; avoid over-red, theatrical, salesy or visually stressful spaces.
Preserve fabric texture, skin truth, daylight variation and natural shadows in retouching; do not use plastic skin, fake glow, artificial blur or over-saturated red.
Red is punctuation, not flood: use it for logo, product tag, CTA, detail line or a single accent only.
Do not place red curtains, red bedding, red props or red outfits into room scenes.
Avoid starbursts, heavy badges, excess CTAs, over-red backgrounds and competing claims.
Use clean sans-serif hierarchy; headlines should breathe and proof should stay ordered.
Identify the brand with confidence and restraint; the logo should not behave like wallpaper.

preserve: Motivating Reset as the core strategic essence.
Designed to De-Stress as the public philosophy.
Warm, domestic, tactile environments with a calm central product.
Controlled red as a recognisable brand signal.
Believable body language and relaxed homewear.
Visible product texture, seams and material honesty.
explore: A compact connected everyday home with clear circulation.
A garden-threshold reset with framed greenery and strong daylight.
A warm architectural social lounge for sofas and motion pieces.
A sheltered reading/recovery corner for recliners and recovery products.
A source-shot system that scales cleanly across brand, product, digital, retail and sale modes.
avoid: Treating the brand like a generic mattress company.
Over-red rooms, red bedding, red props or red outfits.
Presenter poses, forced smiles and camera-selling body language.
Plastic retouching, fake glow, blur masks or invented atmosphere inside photographs.
Using strategy copy as proof of product efficacy.
unknowns: Final production logo, wordmark, tagline lockup and typeface are unresolved across sources.
Exact SKU/variant, dimensions, mechanism clearances and approved claim pack are not supplied here.
Whether Restore, Recharge, Oasis, Recalibrate and Neuma are fully adopted portfolio names remains unresolved.
Exact palette values or hex codes are not provided and should not be invented.
Product-specific efficacy, health or performance claims need current approved substantiation.
guide.decisionSummary: Use the draft and strategy sources as directional guidance for a calm, warm domestic reset world. Keep Duroflex red controlled, keep people believable, keep product truth intact, and do not treat the positioning as proof. Final identity masters, portfolio adoption and approved claims still need confirmation before production.
